paragraphs.source_en: Nevertheless, because experiments confirm that quantum mechanics does describe fundamental physics, it presents a frontal assault on our basic beliefs as to what constitutes reality. Einstein, in particular, was deeply troubled by the probabilistic character of quantum theory. Physics, he would emphasize again and again, is in the business of determining with certainty what has happened, what is happening, and what will happen in the world around us. Physicists are not bookies, and physics is not the business of calculat ing odds. But Einstein could not deny that quantum mechanics was enor mously successful in explaining and predicting, albeit in a statistical framework, experimental observations of the microworld.
